editorial:
Ever feel like you can never really escape your parents' drama? You will totally relate to the main character here, a guy who is still stuck in the middle of his parents' messy divorce even though it happened fifteen years ago. The whole vibe is light and funny, focusing on the awkwardness of family fights that never seem to end. Things get really wild when he finds out he was actually part of a secret psychological study as a kid. Now that he is an adult, the researchers want him back for a follow-up, which just adds more fuel to the fire and makes his home life even more chaotic.

What really makes this work is how the actors nail those cringey family moments that feel way too real. The pacing is quick, and while the plot is simple, the jokes land well. Some parts might feel a bit slow, but it is mostly a smooth ride. You should definitely check this out if you like comedies about dysfunctional families. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: In the end, the main character finally stops trying to fix his parents' relationship and realizes he cannot change them. He uses the results of the study to confront both of them about their behavior. He stops being the middleman and sets firm boundaries. This allows him to move forward with his own life and find peace. The movie wraps up with the family accepting that they will never be perfect, but they can at least be civil.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves relatable family comedies and stories about growing up.
